newsitem.title: UK: Laura Ashley bounces after trading statement.
newsitem.headline: Laura Ashley bounces after trading statement.

text.p: Shares in Laura Ashley Holdings Plc advanced on Tuesday after a trading statement from the British retailer proved less gloomy than some investors had expected, dealers said.
The company said it expected a first-half pretax loss of about 4.5 million stg, including a charge for closing two factories. It predicted breakeven full-year pretax figures.
Dealers said that although the news was not welcome, the shares had already dived on Monday on newspaper reports of the impending profit warning so had fallen far enough.
"The news was priced in so today if anything there was just a sense of relief that it is out of the way," one market-maker said.
The shares were up 1-1/2p at 58 by 0911 GMT in thin volume of around 243,000 shares.
"It is a pretty miserable performance and will increase the pressure on the management," said Nick Bubb, analyst at SocGen.
The company said its lower-than-expected profits were due to slower sales, particularly in the U.S.
"America is clearly the major problem," Bubb said. "Ann Iverson put a lot of her personal stock of credibility into the American expansion programme so she clearly is under a lot of pressure."
Bubb said he was disappointed by the company's predictions for the second half.
"A loss of that order of magnitude in the first half is not much of a surprise but the second half is clearly a big disappointment," he said.
"They have had quite good sales figures but the sting in the tail is the huge fall in their gross margin in the first half."
